name: Purandara
dates_notes: Purandara is known only through later citation and report; the proposed early-medieval placement is approximate and is not supported by an independent biography.
evidence_basis: Named position preserved in later philosophical discussion, especially reports cited in commentarial debate.
own_corpus_survival: No independent work survives; the position is recoverable only from citations and reports.
core_thesis: Purandara is a fragmentarily preserved Cārvāka voice credited with distinguishing ordinary inference from claims about imperceptible entities. In reports of his position, inference may be used provisionally in practical and empirically testable contexts, while purported inferences to an unseen afterlife, karma, or supersensible reality remain unwarranted. This qualification is important because it prevents the Cārvāka tradition from being reduced to the blanket claim that all inference is impossible; the surviving evidence is nevertheless indirect and too slight to support a fuller reconstruction.
